content: 1. Flucytosine and tenofovir DF should be monitored closely as they can increase each other's toxicity through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Flucytosine raises tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Exercise caution and monitor carefully. 2. Tenofovir DF and flurbiprofen should be monitored closely as they can elevate each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 3. Co-administration of tenofovir DF with other drugs primarily excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, such as high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs, may result in toxicity. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 4. Fosphenytoin and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Foscarnet and tenofovir DF both elevate the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Fostamatinib increases tenofovir DF levels or effects by reducing its metabolism. Concomitant use may also raise concentrations of BCRP substrate drugs. Monitor for toxicities of BCRP substrates, and dosage reduction may be required. 7. Ganciclovir increases tenofovir DF levels through mechanisms involving renal function reduction or competition for active tubular secretion. Monitor closely and use caution. 8. Gentamicin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Gentamicin raises tenofovir DF levels by decreasing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases tenofovir DF levels or effects by reducing its metabolism. Plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates may also rise. Monitor closely and use caution. 10. Tenofovir DF and ibuprofen can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 11. Indinavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Tenofovir DF and indomethacin can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 13. Istradefylline increases tenofovir DF levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Clinical trials have shown increased peak levels and AUC of P-gp substrates. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates and monitor closely. 14. Tenofovir DF and ketoprofen can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 15. Tenofovir DF and ketorolac can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 16. Lamivudine and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Lasmiditan increases tenofovir DF levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition and other mechanisms. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lasmiditan inhibits BCRP in vitro, and co-administration with BCRP substrates should be avoided. 18. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases tenofovir DF levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition and unspecified mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Leniolisib increases tenofovir DF levels or effects through BCRP inhibition, potentially increasing systemic exposure to BCRP substrates. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 20. Tenofovir DF decreases letermovir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter induction. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 21. Lonafarnib increases tenofovir DF levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Monitor for adverse reactions, and reduce P-gp substrate doses if needed. 22. Tenofovir DF and lovotibeglogene autotemcel should not be co-administered. Discontinue antiretrovirals at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. ARTs may interfere with lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing. 23. Mavorixafor increases tenofovir DF levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Monitor closely and use caution. 24. Tenofovir DF and meclofenamate can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 25. Tenofovir DF and mefenamic acid can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 26. Tenofovir DF and meloxicam can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 27. Tenofovir DF increases memantine levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 28. Tenofovir DF increases metformin levels by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of lactic acidosis. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Tenofovir DF increases midodrine levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 30. Mitomycin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Mitomycin raises tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Tenofovir DF increases morphine levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 32. Tenofovir DF and nabumetone can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 33. Tenofovir DF and naproxen can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 34. Nelfinavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Neomycin PO and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Neomycin PO raises tenofovir DF levels by decreasing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Nevirapine and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Tenofovir DF decreases nintedanib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter induction. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 38. Orlistat decreases tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if increased HIV viral load is confirmed. 39. Otesaconazole increases tenofovir DF levels or effects through BCRP inhibition. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or consider reducing their dose. Monitor closely. 40. Oxaliplatin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The combination may also raise tenofovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Tenofovir DF and oxaprozin can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 42. Pamidronate increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. The combination may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Paromomycin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Paromomycin raises tenofovir DF levels by decreasing elimination. Monitor closely. 44. Pemetrexed and tenofovir DF can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Both drugs also increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Penicillamine and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Penicillamine raises tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Pentamidine and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The combination may also raise tenofovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Tenofovir DF increases peramivir levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution when peramivir is co-administered with nephrotoxic drugs. Monitor closely. 48. Tenofovir DF and piroxicam can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 49. Tenofovir DF increases pramipexole levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 50. Probenecid increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 51. Tenofovir DF increases procainamide levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 52. Tenofovir DF and quinidine can elevate each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Regorafenib increases tenofovir DF levels or effects through BCRP inhibition. Co-administration with BCRP substrates may increase systemic exposure and related toxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 54. Ritonavir increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Safinamide increases tenofovir DF levels or effects through intestinal BCRP inhibition. Monitor BCRP substrates for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Sarecycline increases tenofovir DF levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates, and dosage reduction may be required when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 57. Sirolimus and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Sirolimus raises tenofovir DF levels. Use caution and monitor closely.
